hero.headline: Fetterman opposes Blanche confirmation for attorney general
hero.body:
Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania announced Thursday that he would vote against confirming Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche as the permanent head of the Justice Department. The Democratic senator made his position known to reporters gathered outside the Capitol.

Fetterman's declaration adds to mounting Democratic criticism of President Trump's expected nomination of Blanche for the role. The senator pointed to Blanche's efforts to establish a controversial fund as a key reason for his opposition.

Trump indicated his intention to nominate Blanche permanently to the position, telling Pod Force One podcast that he believed Blanche "will" become attorney general. "He's a very talented guy," Trump said, noting that Blanche was "doing a very good job" at the Justice Department. Blanche, a longtime Trump ally and former personal lawyer, was appointed to the acting position in April following Trump's firing of Pam Bondi.

Since taking the helm of the Justice Department, Blanche has overseen a series of actions that have drawn criticism. These include filing criminal charges against former FBI Director James Comey, escalating investigations into former CIA Director John Brennan, and removing press releases related to prosecutions of people involved in the January 6 Capitol riot.

One particularly controversial initiative involved Blanche's effort to establish an $1.8 billion fund to compensate Trump's allies, including those who participated in the Capitol attack. The plan sparked immediate legal challenges and fierce political opposition, including from Senate Republicans who objected to using taxpayer money to reimburse January 6 rioters. Blanche abruptly canceled the fund on Tuesday amid widespread condemnation.

Trump defended the proposed compensation during his podcast interview, characterizing the potential recipients as victims of political persecution. "These are people that have been decimated," he said. "There's never been anything like this, what happened to those people, and these were many great people."

The attorney general position serves as the nation's chief law enforcement officer and heads the Justice Department. Any confirmation of Blanche would require a simple majority vote in the Senate. With growing Democratic opposition and Fetterman's public declaration against confirmation, the Trump administration could face significant obstacles to securing Senate approval.

Blanche has also confirmed that the federal government maintains an agreement preventing the Internal Revenue Service from auditing Trump, his family, and related entities, according to statements he made during a House appropriations committee hearing.

The Senate has not yet scheduled a confirmation hearing for Blanche. Should Trump formally nominate him, the Judiciary Committee would hold hearings before the full Senate votes on the appointment.

cards.headline: Hezbollah Rejects Cease-Fire Between Israel and Lebanon
cards.body:
A cease-fire agreement between Israel and the Lebanese government has collapsed after Hezbollah rejected the terms. The United States announced the deal following fresh rounds of direct talks between Israeli and Lebanese diplomats, but the Iran-backed group was not included in the negotiations and refuses to accept the agreement.

Hezbollah's leader, Naim Qassem, called the plan a "roadmap to annihilate part of the Lebanese people" in a statement. He demanded a complete ceasefire and the withdrawal of Israeli troops from Lebanon. Qassem said that as long as Lebanese villages were being bombed, northern Israel would not be safe, and that the resistance would continue as long as occupation existed. He criticized the direct negotiations between the Lebanese and Israeli governments as "a farce and humiliation."

The cease-fire called for Hezbollah to halt its attacks and pull all fighters south of the Litani River, while Israel would end its military operations. The Lebanese government has been negotiating with Israel in an effort to reassert control over the country and disarm Hezbollah, but the group operates independently and maintains significant military capabilities.

The Lebanese prime minister, Nawaf Salam, said those who delayed or rejected a ceasefire would bear responsibility for the consequences. He described the negotiation track as the fastest and least costly option for Lebanon and its residents.

Iran also rejected the ceasefire shortly after it was announced. The head of Iran's Quds Force stated that Israel should withdraw to its prewar positions, calling the removal of Israel from the region "an attainable goal for Muslims." Iran's foreign ministry said Lebanon must be an integral part of any ceasefire and final agreement.

Fighting continued on Thursday despite the ceasefire announcement. Israel carried out airstrikes in southern Lebanon and the Bekaa valley, killing four people. Hezbollah claimed it targeted Israeli soldiers in southern Lebanon. Israel's defense minister said his country had freedom of action to strike Beirut in response to attacks on Israeli communities.

The breakdown represents a significant setback for U.S. diplomatic efforts in the region. It highlights the complexity of negotiating peace when key parties are excluded from talks. The Lebanese government has limited ability to enforce terms that Hezbollah opposes, and the group functions as both a political party and an armed militia within Lebanon.

Israeli troops currently control more than 600 square kilometers of territory in southern Lebanon and have destroyed dozens of border villages. Lebanon and Israel have also agreed to establish pilot zones where Lebanese armed forces would take exclusive control of territory to exclude non-state actors. The failure of this ceasefire sets the stage for continued hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah along the Lebanese border.

cards.headline: Jobless Claims Rise to Highest Level Since February
cards.teaser: Applications for unemployment benefits in the United States increased to 225,000 last week, marking the highest level since February when the Iran war began.
cards.body:
Applications for unemployment benefits in the United States increased to 225,000 last week, marking the highest level since February when the Iran war began. The rise in weekly jobless claims provides a measure of layoff activity across the country and represents a notable uptick in workers seeking aid.

The increase came during a holiday week, which can affect the typical pattern of claims filings. Weekly jobless claims serve as a proxy for layoffs and offer insight into the health of the labor market. The February comparison point coincides with the start of military conflict with Iran, a period that brought economic uncertainty to markets and businesses.

Despite the jump to a four-month high, some analysts caution against reading too much into the single-week data. Holiday weeks often produce irregular patterns in labor market statistics as businesses adjust schedules and workers take time off. The claims data will need to be monitored in coming weeks to determine whether this represents a meaningful shift in labor market conditions or a temporary fluctuation.

The rise in jobless claims comes as other economic indicators show mixed signals. Stock markets have shown volatility, with sector rotation seeing investors move money from technology stocks into banks and retail. Worker productivity data was also revised downward, suggesting efficiency gains may be slowing. The Federal Reserve and policymakers will be watching labor market data closely as they assess the broader economic picture and potential policy responses.

The labor market has remained relatively resilient throughout recent economic challenges, but the uptick in unemployment applications will draw attention from economists and business leaders. The data arrives at a time when businesses are navigating ongoing geopolitical tensions and shifting consumer demand patterns across sectors.

cards.headline: John Bolton to plead guilty to retaining classified information
cards.teaser: The former national security advisor reached a plea agreement with prosecutors over mishandling national security documents.
cards.body:
John Bolton, the former national security adviser who became a prominent critic of President Trump, has reached a plea agreement in a case charging him with mishandling classified documents. Under the deal, Bolton will plead guilty to one count of illegal retention of sensitive national security information.

As part of the agreement, Bolton must pay a $2.25 million fine. The plea deal is subject to court approval and brings resolution to a Justice Department case filed against him in 2025.

cards.headline: Ultra-Orthodox Protesters Riot in Israel Over Military Draft
cards.teaser: Escalating protests by Haredim against mandatory military service have exposed deepening divisions ahead of national elections.
cards.body:
Ultra-Orthodox Jews in Israel have escalated protests against military service requirements in recent weeks, with demonstrations turning to riots. The Haredim community has long resisted mandatory conscription, and the latest unrest has shocked many Israelis.

The protests underscore growing divisions within Israeli society as the country approaches national elections. Military service has been a persistent point of tension between secular Israelis, who are required to serve, and ultra-Orthodox communities, who have historically received exemptions for religious study.

cards.headline: Supreme Court Rules SEC Can Collect Illegal Gains Without Proving Victim Loss
cards.teaser: The justices unanimously sided with the Securities and Exchange Commission in a case about the agency's enforcement powers.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court unanimously sided with the Securities and Exchange Commission, ruling that the agency can recover profits from securities law violations without proving that specific victims suffered financial losses. The decision expands the SEC's enforcement authority by allowing it to strip wrongdoers of ill-gotten gains regardless of demonstrable victim harm.

The ruling clarifies the scope of the SEC's power to pursue financial misconduct cases. By backing the agency's position, the justices affirmed that the SEC has discretion in recovering illegal profits without the additional burden of documenting individual victim losses.

cards.headline: Supreme Court Backs Trump Administration on Telecom Regulation
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court sided with the Trump administration in a case involving federal regulation of telecommunications companies.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court ruled 8-1 in favor of the Federal Communications Commission's authority to impose fines on wireless carriers through in-house proceedings. AT&T and Verizon had challenged the system, arguing it violated their constitutional right to a jury trial. The justices rejected this claim, upholding the FCC's enforcement powers.

The decision represents a victory for the Trump administration's approach to telecommunications regulation. The ruling affirms the agency's ability to levy penalties against major carriers without requiring a jury trial.

cards.headline: Marjane Satrapi, Author of Persepolis, Dies at 56
cards.teaser: The Iranian-French author and illustrator created a graphic novel series that followed a girl through the Islamic Revolution and Iran-Iraq War.
cards.body:
Marjane Satrapi, the French-Iranian author and illustrator of the acclaimed graphic novel series Persepolis, has died at age 56. Her landmark autobiographical work, published in the early 2000s, followed an Iranian girl through the Islamic Revolution and the Iran-Iraq War, helping reshape international perceptions of Iran.

According to her family, Satrapi died of sadness following the death of her husband, Swedish producer Mattias Ripa, last year. The Persepolis series became a significant work in graphic literature, and the film adaptation received an Oscar nomination.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak Spreads Amid Mistrust in Congo Mining Town
cards.teaser: Health workers in a remote area of the Democratic Republic of Congo face resistance from residents who deny the disease is real.
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in a remote mining town in the Democratic Republic of Congo is being hampered by community skepticism. Some residents deny the disease exists, complicating efforts by health workers to treat patients and safely manage burials.

The outbreak has exposed a critical gap in disease preparedness: there is an effective Ebola vaccine, but not for the strain currently spreading in Congo. Multiple vaccine candidates are undergoing trials, though their timelines remain uncertain. Meanwhile, health workers continue navigating logistical challenges and community resistance in the isolated area to contain transmission.

cards.headline: Ultra-Orthodox Protesters Riot in Israel Over Military Draft
cards.teaser: Escalating protests by Haredim against mandatory military service have exposed deepening divisions ahead of national elections.

cards.headline: New Zealand Lawmakers Banned From China After Taiwan Visit
cards.teaser: Four members of parliament received one-year travel bans, marking a shift in how China responds to such visits.
cards.body:
China has banned four New Zealand lawmakers from entering the country for one year following their visit to Taiwan last month. New Zealand's foreign minister expressed surprise at the restriction, noting that lawmakers have traveled to Taiwan in the past without triggering such consequences.

The ban signals a shift in China's approach to foreign officials visiting Taiwan, which Beijing claims as its own territory. While China typically objects to diplomatic contact between other nations and Taiwan, it had previously allowed New Zealand officials to visit without imposing formal travel restrictions.

cards.headline: Young Chinese Learn About Tiananmen Square Despite Censorship
cards.teaser: On the anniversary of the crackdown, information about the 1989 protests continues to reach younger generations in China.
cards.body:
Young people in China are learning about the Tiananmen Square crackdown despite government censorship efforts. The anniversary of the 1989 protests has prompted renewed attention to how information about the event spreads within the country.

Police have warned families of those killed in the crackdown not to visit graves on the 37th anniversary. China and the United States clashed over the commemoration, while Taiwan called on China to face the historical record. Activists continue working to preserve the memory of the protests and the government's response.

cards.headline: Dutch Police Investigate Suspected Drugging and Sexual Assaults
cards.teaser: Authorities raided suspects' homes after receiving information from German and UK police about multiple women targeted.
cards.body:
Dutch police have launched an investigation into suspected drugging and sexual assault targeting multiple women. Acting on tip-offs from German and UK law enforcement agencies, authorities conducted raids on the homes of suspects.

The investigation reflects cross-border police coordination, with authorities in the Netherlands responding to information from their counterparts in Germany and the United Kingdom that suggested connections between the suspected crimes across European nations.

cards.teaser: Staff at the performing arts center received instructions to immediately strip the former president's name from official materials.
cards.body:
The John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts directed employees to remove references to Trump's name from center documents. The order requires staff to complete the changes by June 12, affecting various official materials and records at the Washington cultural institution.

The Kennedy Center serves as the national performing arts venue and receives federal funding while operating under a nonprofit structure. The directive reflects ongoing legal and administrative actions involving Trump's name on federal properties and institutions.

cards.headline: Senate rejects Democratic amendment to block Justice Department payout fund
cards.teaser: Republicans defeated an attempt to ban a fund Trump established to compensate individuals who claim government wrongdoing.
cards.body:
The Senate voted down a Democratic amendment seeking to eliminate a Justice Department fund designed to compensate individuals who claim improper treatment by federal investigators. The vote took place during Senate consideration of legislation funding Immigration and Customs Enforcement and border operations.

The fund has become a flashpoint in debates over Justice Department oversight. Democrats have opposed it, raising concerns about accountability and potential misuse. This comes after acting attorney general Todd Blanche told lawmakers the DOJ was not moving forward with the fund, though Republicans voted to preserve it.

cards.headline: Hezbollah rejects new Lebanon ceasefire agreement
cards.teaser: The militant group declined a truce announced by the United States after negotiations between Israel and Lebanon.
cards.body:
Hezbollah rejected a ceasefire agreement announced by the United States on Wednesday night following diplomatic talks between Israel and Lebanon. The rejection threatens to prolong the conflict in the region and undermines American efforts to broker peace in the area.

The rejection comes as violence continues to affect the region. A U.N. peacekeeper was killed and others were wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon, according to UNIFIL, the U.N. peacekeeping mission operating there.

cards.headline: Royal Navy identifies three crew members killed in helicopter crash
cards.teaser: The Ministry of Defence released the names of service members who died in a naval aviation accident.
cards.body: The Royal Navy has named three crew members killed in a helicopter crash: Lieutenant Commander Chris Gayson, 42, Lieutenant Lily-Mae Fisher, 31, and Petty Officer Owen Green, 24. Tributes have been paid to the service members following the fatal accident.

cards.headline: Staff member shot with crossbow at university campus
cards.teaser: A university employee was attacked at the Guildford campus in an incident under police investigation.
cards.body:
A staff member at a university in Guildford was shot with a crossbow on campus during an attack Thursday morning. The university confirmed the incident occurred on the Guildford campus and that emergency services responded to the scene.

Authorities are investigating the circumstances of the attack. The use of a crossbow in the assault represents an uncommon form of violence on a university campus, where security concerns typically focus on other threats.

cards.headline: British lawyer reports ex-wife of Dubai ruler's nephew missing
cards.teaser: David Haigh lost contact with Zeynab Javadli and found her Dubai home locked and empty.
cards.body:
British lawyer David Haigh has reported that Zeynab Javadli, ex-wife of a nephew of Dubai's ruler, is missing. Haigh lost contact with Javadli on Tuesday. Her home in Dubai is locked and appears empty, according to sources who spoke to the BBC.

Haigh, who serves as Javadli's legal representative, reported her disappearance after being unable to reach his client.

hero.headline: Dow Gains 800 Points as Investors Shift From Tech to Banks and Retail
hero.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 800 points while the Nasdaq lagged as investors rotated money out of semiconductor stocks.
hero.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged more than 800 points to reach record territory as investors redirected capital away from semiconductor stocks and into banking and retail shares. The shift reflected a broader rotation out of technology names that had dominated market gains in recent months.

The S&P 500 also advanced, while the Nasdaq moved higher despite weakness in its technology-heavy concentration. Oil prices declined following announcements of an Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, providing support across the broader market.

The sector rotation was triggered by earnings reports from major chipmakers. Broadcom's disappointing results prompted investors to reassess their positions in artificial intelligence-related stocks, with the company joining Micron and ARM Holdings in posting significant declines. Ciena also dropped after reporting earnings, adding to weakness in technology infrastructure stocks.

The market movement underscored investor appetite for areas beyond the concentrated technology sector. After an extended period where artificial intelligence stocks drove market gains, traders appeared ready to explore opportunities elsewhere. Banking and retail stocks benefited from this reallocation of funds.

The pullback in semiconductor shares reflected caution about valuations and growth expectations in the chip sector. While technology stocks had delivered substantial returns, some investors took Broadcom's results as a signal to lock in profits and move money into areas that had lagged during the tech-driven rally.

The decline in oil prices supported stock market sentiment more broadly. Crude prices fell as markets processed the geopolitical implications of the ceasefire announcement in the Middle East, reducing concerns about potential supply disruptions.

Despite the technology weakness, the Nasdaq's ability to finish higher demonstrated that not all tech-related stocks suffered during the day's trading. Some areas of the technology sector maintained strength, even as semiconductor and AI-focused names retreated.

The strong showing by the Dow suggested that blue-chip stocks, including financial institutions and consumer-focused companies, attracted significant buying interest. This pattern indicated that investors were not necessarily becoming bearish on equities overall but were instead recalibrating their portfolio exposure to different sectors.

The market action reflected normal dynamics where periods of strong performance in specific sectors eventually give way to rotation as investors reassess risk and return opportunities. The shift from chips to banks and retail suggested confidence in economic fundamentals while acknowledging that recent technology gains had become stretched.

Analysts watching the market noted that such rotations were typical as investors continuously rebalanced their holdings. The ability of the market's broad indexes to gain ground despite technology weakness provided evidence that the underlying strength of equities remained intact, even as attention shifted away from the names that had led the previous period of gains.

cards.headline: Quantinuum Opens at $68 in Quantum Computing IPO
cards.teaser: Quantinuum stock began trading at $68 per share after its initial public offering, with shares jumping 13 percent from the IPO price.
cards.body:
Quantinuum, a quantum computing company backed by Honeywell, saw its shares open at $68 in its stock market debut. The IPO was oversubscribed 20 times, reflecting strong investor demand for quantum computing technology. Shares rose 13 percent from the offering price in early trading, marking a successful public market entry for the sector.

The debut represents a significant moment for quantum computing companies entering public markets. The company's IPO was upsized to meet investor demand, and the opening drew attention from investors looking for exposure to emerging computing technologies. The strong reception comes amid broader market rotation and interest in technology beyond traditional semiconductor plays.

cards.headline: Scott Pelley Fired From 60 Minutes Amid News Division Turmoil
cards.teaser: CBS fired veteran journalist Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes, the latest staffing change at the network's news division.
cards.body:
CBS fired veteran journalist Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes on Tuesday, escalating turmoil within the network's news division. Pelley subsequently accused the network's new executives of instructing him to inject "falsehoods and bias" into his reporting and of silencing employees.

In a public statement, Pelley emphasized that 60 Minutes has maintained its decades-long position as America's top program through integrity and quality journalism. His firing represents the latest in a series of staffing departures and controversies affecting CBS News as the division navigates changes in leadership and editorial direction.

cards.headline: Gwynne Shotwell Leads SpaceX Operations Ahead of Planned IPO
cards.teaser: SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell manages day-to-day operations as the company prepares to go public.
cards.body:
Gwynne Shotwell serves as president and chief operating officer of SpaceX, functioning as a steady operational counterbalance to Elon Musk. While Musk focuses on broader vision and other ventures, Shotwell manages the company's day-to-day business operations.

SpaceX is preparing for a major initial public offering, with Shotwell overseeing the company's satellite launches, spacecraft development, and commercial contracts. Her leadership has been central to executing SpaceX's operational goals as the company moves toward going public.

hero.headline: Helion raises $465 million to build fusion power plant for Microsoft
hero.body:
Helion, a fusion energy startup backed by OpenAI chief Sam Altman, has secured $465 million in new funding to construct a power plant for Microsoft. The company aims to complete the facility by 2028 under a power purchase agreement with the technology company.

Fusion energy represents a potential clean power source that generates electricity by fusing atomic nuclei, mimicking the process that powers the sun. Unlike traditional nuclear fission plants, fusion produces no long-lived radioactive waste and carries minimal meltdown risk. Despite decades of research, the technology has remained commercially unproven, with no fusion plant yet delivering net energy to the grid at scale.

Helion employs a pulsed non-ignition fusion system that heats plasma to extremely high temperatures. While the company has demonstrated technical progress recently, significant engineering challenges remain before prototype reactors can be scaled into functioning power plants. The Microsoft agreement marks one of the first major corporate commitments to purchase fusion-generated electricity, even as the technology remains unproven commercially.

The 2028 deadline presents an aggressive timeline for the fusion industry. Most fusion projects have historically experienced delays, and experts caution that delivering grid-ready power within such a compressed timeframe would require overcoming substantial technical and regulatory obstacles. The new capital will support construction activities and equipment procurement as Helion works to meet its contractual deadlines.

Microsoft has been actively investing in alternative energy sources to power its expanding data center operations while meeting climate goals. The company has signed multiple renewable energy deals in recent years, including contracts for solar and wind power. The Helion partnership demonstrates growing corporate appetite for next-generation energy technologies, particularly as companies seek solutions to power the massive computational demands of artificial intelligence systems.

The surge in interest around fusion energy reflects broader industry concerns about electricity demand. Data centers required for AI applications consume enormous amounts of power, prompting major technology companies to explore diverse energy sources. Nuclear power, including both traditional reactors and emerging fusion technologies, has attracted renewed attention as companies balance operational needs with environmental commitments.

Helion's $465 million funding round strengthens its position in a competitive fusion landscape. Multiple companies are pursuing fusion technology through different approaches, backed by significant capital and institutional support. While fusion remains developmental, corporate partnerships like the Microsoft deal signal that investors and major enterprises increasingly view the technology as potentially viable for meeting future energy demands.

The coming years will test whether Helion and similar companies can translate technical advances into commercial reality. Success would represent a landmark moment for fusion energy, potentially opening a new chapter in how industries power computationally intensive operations while reducing carbon emissions.

cards.headline: Ramp raises $750 million at $44 billion valuation
cards.teaser: The expense management startup has nearly tripled its valuation over the past year as investors focus on fintech companies with artificial intelligence capabilities.
cards.body:
Ramp secured $750 million in funding at a $44 billion valuation, nearly tripling its worth over the past year. The funding round underscores strong investor demand for fintech startups, particularly those integrating artificial intelligence into their platforms.

The expense management platform's rapid growth reflects broader market enthusiasm for automation in corporate finance. Investors are actively competing to back fast-growing startups in the space as AI-driven financial tools gain traction with businesses.

cards.headline: Meta Oversight Board criticizes account ban process for lacking transparency
cards.teaser: The independent board says Meta fails to provide clear information about violations and how artificial intelligence is used in enforcement decisions.
cards.body:
Meta's Oversight Board has criticized the company's account suspension process, citing concerns over due process and transparency. The board is calling on Meta to provide users with clearer information about policy violations when their accounts are banned.

The board is also pressing Meta to be more transparent about how it uses artificial intelligence in content moderation and account enforcement decisions. This comes as Meta increasingly relies on automated systems to manage content across its platforms.

cards.headline: NASA's MAVEN spacecraft ends 11-year Mars mission
cards.teaser: The Mars orbiter ceased operations after more than a decade studying the planet's atmosphere and climate history.
cards.body:
NASA's MAVEN spacecraft concluded its mission at Mars after 11 years of operations studying the planet's upper atmosphere. The orbiter had been collecting data on how Mars lost much of its atmosphere over billions of years, transforming from a potentially habitable world to the cold, dry planet seen today.

Mission team members described the end of operations as the loss of a loved one. MAVEN arrived at Mars in 2014 and exceeded its planned mission duration by several years, providing scientists with extensive measurements of atmospheric escape processes and solar wind interactions.

cards.headline: Apple prepares Siri overhaul and AI updates for WWDC conference
cards.teaser: The company is expected to unveil a revamped voice assistant and new Apple Intelligence features at its annual developer event.
cards.body:
Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference is approaching, with the company preparing to announce a significant Siri redesign and updates to its Apple Intelligence platform. The voice assistant has faced criticism for lagging behind competitors in capabilities and accuracy.

The anticipated Siri changes represent Apple's latest push to improve its artificial intelligence offerings after facing pressure from rival products. The company has been working to integrate more advanced language processing and expand Siri's functionality across its device ecosystem.

cards.headline: Meta launches AI assistant to help creators track performance
cards.teaser: Facebook creators can now ask an artificial intelligence tool questions about posting times and audience engagement instead of reviewing analytics dashboards.
cards.body:
Meta has rolled out an AI-powered assistant for Facebook creators that answers questions about content performance and audience behavior in conversational language. Rather than manually reviewing analytics dashboards, creators can now ask questions like "When should I post?" or "What are people saying in my comments?" to get quick insights.

The assistant is designed to save creators time by streamlining how they interpret performance data across multiple platforms. Instead of spending hours analyzing charts to understand reach and engagement patterns, they can receive immediate answers about content strategy and audience response.

cards.headline: Waymo to repurpose robotaxi batteries for grid storage
cards.teaser: The autonomous vehicle company announced a partnership to convert spent battery packs from its fleet into stationary energy storage systems.
cards.body:
Waymo announced a partnership with B2U Storage Solutions to repurpose battery packs from its robotaxis as grid-scale energy storage. The batteries will be reused once they're retired from vehicle service, extending their useful life and reducing waste from the autonomous vehicle fleet.

This approach takes advantage of the fact that electric vehicle batteries retain significant capacity after they no longer meet the performance requirements for transportation. The repurposed batteries can then store renewable energy and support grid stability for several additional years before eventual recycling.

hero.headline: Green Bay signs Christian Watson to four-year, $110.5 million extension
hero.teaser: The Packers locked up their star wide receiver with a deal that includes a $31 million signing bonus.
hero.body:
Wide receiver Christian Watson and the Green Bay Packers agreed to a four-year contract extension worth $110.5 million, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Thursday. The deal includes a $31 million signing bonus.

The extension secures Watson's future with the Packers through the 2030 season. Watson has emerged as a key target in Green Bay's passing attack since joining the team.

cards.headline: NBA issues lifetime bans to two fans after Finals court intrusion
cards.teaser: The NBA banned two fans for life from all league arenas following an incident during Game 1 of the NBA Finals on Wednesday night.
cards.body:
The NBA banned two fans for life from all league arenas following a selfie-seeking incident during Game 1 of the NBA Finals on Wednesday night. A league spokesperson confirmed the action Thursday, describing the episode as a courtside intrusion that disrupted play.

Lifetime bans represent the league's most severe penalty for spectators, preventing individuals from attending any NBA game at any league-operated or affiliated arena. The swift action underscores the NBA's commitment to maintaining security boundaries during the championship series.

cards.headline: Liverpool hires Andoni Iraola as head coach
cards.teaser: The club confirmed Iraola will replace Arne Slot on a two-year contract.
cards.body:
Liverpool appointed Andoni Iraola as their new head coach on a two-year contract, replacing Arne Slot who was sacked six days earlier. The 43-year-old Spaniard comes to Anfield from Bournemouth, where he previously worked with Liverpool's director of football Richard Hughes.

Liverpool moved quickly to secure Iraola after identifying him as the ideal fit for their preferred playing style. Despite interest from other clubs including Milan, Bayer Leverkusen and Crystal Palace, Iraola was always Liverpool's favoured candidate and the only coach spoken to about the vacancy.

cards.headline: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva advances to French Open final
cards.teaser: Andreeva defeated Marta Kostyuk in straight sets to reach her first Grand Slam final.
cards.body:
Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva advanced to her first Grand Slam final by defeating Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk 6-1, 6-3 in the French Open semifinals. Andreeva's dominant performance saw her control the match from the opening set.

She will face qualifier Maja Chwalinska in the final. Chwalinska secured her spot with a 7-6, 6-4 victory over Diana Shnaider, continuing her remarkable run through the tournament.

cards.headline: Qualifier Maja Chwalinska reaches French Open final
cards.teaser: Chwalinska is one win away from a surprise Grand Slam title after advancing to the final at Roland Garros.
cards.body:
Qualifier Maja Chwalinska advanced to the French Open final with a 7-6, 6-4 victory over Diana Shnaider. She will face Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva, who dominated her semifinal against Marta Kostyuk, winning 6-1, 6-3.

Chwalinska's run to the final is a remarkable achievement. As a qualifier, she had to win preliminary matches just to enter the main draw, and her continued success has positioned her one win away from capturing the Grand Slam title.

cards.headline: Aaron Judge sits for third straight game with rib injury
cards.teaser: The Yankees slugger remained out of the lineup as the team awaits medical information about his condition.
cards.body:
Aaron Judge was out of the New York Yankees lineup on Thursday for a third consecutive game. The team is awaiting clarity about a bone bruise in one of his right ribs that is causing right shoulder pain.

Judge has been sidelined since the injury emerged earlier this week. The Yankees have not provided a timeline for his return as they gather more medical information about the extent of the injury.

cards.headline: World Cup security preparations described as unprecedented challenge
cards.teaser: A White House task force official said law enforcement is preparing for the largest security operation in the tournament's history.
cards.body:
The 2026 World Cup will present an unprecedented security challenge due to its expanded size and scope, according to Andrew Giuliani, executive director of the White House FIFA World Cup 2026 Task Force. Speaking to ESPN, Giuliani said that law enforcement agencies across the nation are actively preparing for the tournament.

The tournament's three-country format—spanning the United States, Canada, and Mexico—creates unique logistical demands. Mexican cities like Monterrey are developing innovative security approaches, including the use of robodogs and helicopters, as they balance World Cup preparations with existing security concerns.

hero.headline: Marjane Satrapi, Author of Persepolis, Dies at 56
hero.body:
Marjane Satrapi, the French-Iranian artist and graphic novelist whose memoir Persepolis transformed international understanding of Iran, has died at 56. Her family stated that she "died of sadness" following the death of her husband, Swedish producer Mattias Ripa, who passed away in April of the previous year. After his death, Satrapi posted on Instagram: "For I lost the love of my life."

Born in 1969 in Rasht, Iran, Satrapi grew up in Tehran with an engineer father and dress designer mother. As a teenager, her parents sent her to Europe to continue her education and escape restrictions under the Islamic Republic. She eventually settled in France, arriving in 1994 and becoming a French citizen in 2006.

Satrapi published Persepolis in 2000 as a comic book memoir that became an international publishing phenomenon. The work tells the story of a rebellious young girl navigating Iran after the shah's overthrow in 1979 and the establishment of the Islamic Republic. It follows her journey through the country's violence and ideological control before her departure to Europe at age 14. The memoir sold millions of copies worldwide and established Satrapi as one of the most widely read Iranian authors globally.

In a 2024 Guardian interview, Satrapi explained that Persepolis aimed to help Western readers recognize the humanity of Iranian people. She initially had modest expectations for the book. "With Persepolis, I didn't even think I'd find a publisher," she told El País in 2020. "I thought I'd make 50 photocopies for my friends to read."

Satrapi co-directed an animated film adaptation of Persepolis, which became an international success and earned her a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature, making her the first woman nominated in that category. She went on to direct five feature films, including Radioactive in 2019, starring Rosamund Pike as Marie Curie.

Throughout her career, Satrapi described drawing as humanity's first language. "Drawing - it's the first language of human beings, before writing, before even talking, before words," she said in a 2012 interview. She emphasized that her work aimed to reassure young Iranians that the outside world heard and supported them.

After leaving comics for years, Satrapi returned to the medium in 2024 by coordinating Woman, Life, Freedom, a collaborative graphic work featuring 17 Iranian and international comic artists alongside academics. The book examined protest movements following the 2022 death in custody of Mahsa Amini, a young Kurdish-Iranian woman. Satrapi stated: "The only thing I can do is cultural work. This book is a message to the Iranian people to say, listen, you are not alone."

President Emmanuel Macron said Satrapi was "a great artist who turned her Iranian childhood into a universal tale," while Margaret Atwood noted that Satrapi had lived the struggles she depicted, making her work increasingly relevant.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift's Net Worth Reaches $2 Billion
cards.teaser: Forbes has added Swift to its Iconoclast 50 list, marking her net worth at $2 billion.
cards.body:
Forbes included Taylor Swift on its Iconoclast 50 list, valuing her net worth at $2 billion. The recognition comes as the music industry has produced legitimate billionaires in recent years, prompting Forbes to expand its coverage accordingly.

Swift has built her wealth through multiple revenue streams, including her music catalog, touring, and business ventures. The $2 billion valuation marks a significant milestone for an artist whose fortune stems primarily from her own creative work and performances.

cards.headline: Bill Ackman to Sell $290.5 Million in Universal Music Stock
cards.teaser: Universal Music will repurchase over 14.2 million shares from Pershing Square after rejecting a takeover proposal.
cards.body:
Universal Music announced it will repurchase over 14.2 million shares from Pershing Square, the capital fund founded and operated by billionaire investor Bill Ackman. The repurchase is worth approximately $290.5 million and represents 250 million euros. The transaction follows Universal Music's rejection of a takeover proposal from Pershing Square.

Universal Music is the world's largest record company. The stock repurchase reduces Pershing Square's stake in the company after the failed acquisition attempt. The transaction represents a significant divestment by Ackman's fund from the music company.

cards.headline: Sadie Sink to Star in FX's The Marriage Plot Limited Series
cards.teaser: FX has greenlit an adaptation of Jeffrey Eugenides' 2011 novel, with production from A24 and direction by Hiro Murai.
cards.body:
FX has ordered The Marriage Plot, a limited series based on Jeffrey Eugenides' 2011 novel. Sadie Sink will star in the project, which is written by Will Arbery and directed by Hiro Murai. The series will stream on Hulu and is produced by A24.

The series follows three recent college graduates caught in a complicated relationship. The adaptation brings together Sink, known for her work in Stranger Things, with Murai, who has directed episodes of Atlanta and The Bear. Arbery's screenplay adapts Eugenides' novel about post-college life and romantic entanglements.

cards.headline: The Beatles to Release All You Need Is Love Performance Clip
cards.teaser: A colorized version of the performance will mark the first time the video has been officially published online.
cards.body:
The Beatles will release a colorized rendition of their All You Need Is Love performance to mark Global Beatles Day. The video will be the first time the performance has been published officially online. The release provides fans with a restored version of a historic Beatles broadcast.

The original All You Need Is Love performance was part of the Our World satellite broadcast in 1967, which reached an estimated 400 million viewers across five continents. The song became one of the band's most recognized anthems. The colorization and official online release makes the performance accessible to contemporary audiences.

cards.headline: Death Boom Documentary to Premiere at Tribeca Festival
cards.teaser: The film from Eli Roth, Jessica Chandler, and Leonardo DiCaprio's Appian Way investigates the end-of-life industry.
cards.body:
A trailer has been released for Death Boom, a documentary exploring the multi-billion dollar death care industry. The film will make its world premiere at the Tribeca Festival on June 9 in New York. Director Jessica Chandler examines end-of-life choices and the impending death boom as the population ages.

The documentary is produced by Eli Roth, Jessica Chandler, and Leonardo DiCaprio's production company Appian Way. The film investigates pressing questions surrounding the death care industry and how Americans navigate end-of-life decisions. The premiere at Tribeca marks the film's first public screening.

cards.headline: Spike Lee and Celebrities Appear in New York Filmmaking PSA
cards.teaser: Mayor Zohran Mamdani's office released a video promoting New York as a filmmaking destination.

hero.headline: Fetterman opposes Blanche confirmation for attorney general
hero.body:
Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania announced Thursday that he would vote against confirming Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche as the permanent head of the Justice Department. The Democratic senator made his position known to reporters gathered outside the Capitol.

Fetterman's declaration adds to mounting Democratic criticism of President Trump's expected nomination of Blanche for the role. The senator pointed to Blanche's efforts to establish a controversial fund as a key reason for his opposition.

Trump indicated his intention to nominate Blanche permanently to the position, telling Pod Force One podcast that he believed Blanche "will" become attorney general. "He's a very talented guy," Trump said, noting that Blanche was "doing a very good job" at the Justice Department. Blanche, a longtime Trump ally and former personal lawyer, was appointed to the acting position in April following Trump's firing of Pam Bondi.

Since taking the helm of the Justice Department, Blanche has overseen a series of actions that have drawn criticism. These include filing criminal charges against former FBI Director James Comey, escalating investigations into former CIA Director John Brennan, and removing press releases related to prosecutions of people involved in the January 6 Capitol riot.

One particularly controversial initiative involved Blanche's effort to establish an $1.8 billion fund to compensate Trump's allies, including those who participated in the Capitol attack. The plan sparked immediate legal challenges and fierce political opposition, including from Senate Republicans who objected to using taxpayer money to reimburse January 6 rioters. Blanche abruptly canceled the fund on Tuesday amid widespread condemnation.

Trump defended the proposed compensation during his podcast interview, characterizing the potential recipients as victims of political persecution. "These are people that have been decimated," he said. "There's never been anything like this, what happened to those people, and these were many great people."

The attorney general position serves as the nation's chief law enforcement officer and heads the Justice Department. Any confirmation of Blanche would require a simple majority vote in the Senate. With growing Democratic opposition and Fetterman's public declaration against confirmation, the Trump administration could face significant obstacles to securing Senate approval.

Blanche has also confirmed that the federal government maintains an agreement preventing the Internal Revenue Service from auditing Trump, his family, and related entities, according to statements he made during a House appropriations committee hearing.

The Senate has not yet scheduled a confirmation hearing for Blanche. Should Trump formally nominate him, the Judiciary Committee would hold hearings before the full Senate votes on the appointment.

cards.headline: Haaland wins Democratic primary for New Mexico governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination for governor of New Mexico.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico on Thursday. She previously served as an official in the Biden administration.

If elected in the general election, Haaland could become the first female Native American governor in United States history. The primary victory positions her as the Democratic candidate to succeed the current governor.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead California gubernatorial primary
cards.teaser: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading in California's open primary to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra are leading their respective party races in California's gubernatorial primary. The contest features Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra competing against Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton.

The primary will determine which candidates advance to the general election to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom. California uses a top-two primary system where the leading candidates from each party typically move forward to the November election.

cards.headline: Senate rejects amendment to redirect Justice Department anti-weaponization funding
cards.teaser: The Senate voted down an amendment that would have redirected $1.8 billion from an anti-weaponization fund to fraud enforcement.
cards.body:
The Senate voted overwhelmingly Thursday to reject an amendment by Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) that would have redirected $1.8 billion in Justice Department funding away from an "anti-weaponization" initiative toward anti-fraud efforts instead.

The amendment would have prohibited federal funds from being used to establish, administer, defend, or support claims related to the anti-weaponization program. This came after acting attorney general Todd Blanche told lawmakers earlier in the week that the DOJ was not moving forward with the fund.

cards.headline: E. Jean Carroll denies perjury allegation amid Justice Department probe
cards.teaser: Writer E. Jean Carroll said she did not commit perjury in response to a reported Justice Department investigation.
cards.body:
E. Jean Carroll responded Thursday to reports of a Justice Department probe into potential perjury allegations. The writer, who accused President Trump of sexual assault, addressed the matter in a post on her Substack platform.

Carroll stated directly that she did not commit perjury. The Justice Department investigation reportedly concerns whether Carroll lied while under oath, though she firmly denied the allegation.

cards.headline: O'Leary agrees to scale back Utah data center project after criticism
cards.teaser: Business mogul Kevin O'Leary said he will reduce the size of his planned 40,000-acre data center campus in Utah.
cards.body:
Kevin O'Leary announced late Wednesday that he would scale back his artificial intelligence data center development in Utah. The Shark Tank investor told NBC News he plans to reduce the size of the 40,000-acre campus.

The decision comes after mounting backlash over the project's size and environmental impact. O'Leary said political pushback prompted his decision to slim down the development.

cards.headline: Republican proposes alternative path for election security legislation
cards.teaser: Rep. Julie Fedorchak offers a new approach to election safeguards as the SAVE America Act stalls in Congress.
cards.body:
With the SAVE America Act stalled in Congress, Rep. Julie Fedorchak is pursuing a different strategy to advance election security measures. Rather than seeking Democratic backing for federal legislation, she is proposing that states adopt their own requirements for REAL ID cards in voting.

This state-level approach would circumvent the need for bipartisan agreement on election legislation at the federal level. The proposal reflects Republican efforts to move forward on election security despite gridlock in Congress.
